Clean and perturbed log-likelihoods, terse vs wordy.

Four columns, same image. The first two share the bare question (clean image vs JPEG-perturbed image); the last two share the wordy-padded question (clean vs same perturbation). The drift label spans the two columns it is computed from — each level's drift uses that level's own clean baseline. The wordy clean log p almost always sits closer to 0 than the terse clean log p, so the smaller wordy drift you see is partly a structural property of the conditioning, not just the spectral filter Wt. The standardised partial regression in the paper is what isolates the filter effect; this panel is the visual hook.

Terse filter Wtterse · IPR bandwidth =

Radially averaged cross-modal attention spectrum at the second-to-last decoder layer (last_2). Narrower ⇒ a single perturbed band can dominate ⟨Wt, ΔF⟩.

Wordy filter Wtwordy · IPR bandwidth =

Same layer, padded prompt. A flatter distribution ⇒ no single band of ΔF dominates ⇒ smaller predicted volatility.

Why are the wordy clean log-probs already so close to 0?

Two confounds are worth disentangling before reading too much into the drift gap:
  • Concern A (reviewer-style): maybe the wordy variant already started lower on the clean baseline ("pre-drifted"), so a small drift just means there is no room left to fall. Empirically falsified in ~99% of cells: wordy clean log p sits higher than terse clean log p, not lower. See scripts/verify_drift_baseline_concerns.py.
  • Concern B (ceiling-style): maybe wordy starts so close to log p = 0 that any perturbation is mechanically compressed. Real, but addressed by the paper's response variable being within-cell volatility (shift-invariant std of drift) and the regression reporting z-scored partial slopes against an attention-derived predictor (first-order overlap or IPR bandwidth) — the slope has no log-prob units at all, so multiplicative compression of drift cancels.
Bottom line: the drift gap shown in this panel is the visual hook; the paper's claim rests on the standardised regression, not raw drift.
How to read. log p are next-token log-likelihoods of each option's text under the model, as logged during inference. Drift is (clean log p) − (perturbed log p) on the gold answer for the same conditioning column — terse drift uses ① − ②, wordy drift uses ③ − ④. IPR bandwidth = inverse participation ratio of the radially averaged cross-modal attention spectrum at last_2; higher means flatter (broader) frequency support. All numbers come from the saved Qwen3-VL-8B 100-sample run with suppress_dc: false.
